customer_ops: Hey support — Private debug bundle generation is failing for customer acme-inc (private deployment). Collector starts, then exits with code 255 during handshake. We captured a request id from the control plane: rqd_8f7b2c4a. Tried to upload debug bundle but presign returns 403. Sharing minimal logs and a curl repro we ran. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: Thanks — can you paste the exact collector version and the collector config (remove any secrets) plus the small log snippet? 403 on presign usually points to a bad IAM role or manifest contents mismatch.

customer_ops: Collector: redwood-collector v2.1.7 (sha: d9a4f). Config: private mode, s3_upload true, upload_dest: s3://acme-debug-bundles, presign=enabled. Log snippet:
```
2028-11-05T14:12:03Z INFO collector starting, config=/etc/redwood/collector.yaml
2028-11-05T14:12:05Z INFO handshake with control-plane ok
2028-11-05T14:12:06Z ERROR upload: presign failed status=403 body={"message":"Access Denied"}
2028-11-05T14:12:06Z ERROR bundle: manifest checksum mismatch expected=6b1e... got=3f2a...
2028-11-05T14:12:06Z FATAL collector exiting code=255
```

alex: That manifest checksum mismatch is interesting — it suggests the collector generated a different manifest than what the control plane expected (maybe redaction removed fields). Did you enable custom redaction rules? Also can you run the collector with DEBUG=collector:upload to get full manifest (no secrets) and paste the manifest JSON (or attach)?

customer_ops: We did enable a site-level redaction config to strip email addresses and some headers. I can spin up a collector with --no-redact to compare. For quick repro, here's the curl we used to hit the presign endpoint (token redacted):
```bash
curl -i -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://control-plane.internal.acme/api/v1/debug/presign \
  -d '{"filename":"bundle-1864006789.tar.gz","size":123456,"checksum":"3f2a...","request_id":"rqd_8f7b2c4a"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 403 {"error":"presign denied","code":"AccessDenied"}

maria: Quick checklist: (1) ensure the IAM role the control plane uses to presign has PutObject on the target prefix; (2) confirm the manifest checksum algorithm (sha256 vs md5) matches between collector and control plane; (3) check that redaction isn't modifying fields included in the checksum (e.g., timestamps).

sam: For reproducing locally: try running the collector with exact same config but add env var REDWOOD_NO_REDACT=1 and run the debug upload flow to see if checksum aligns. Also run the presign curl but change checksum to the one the collector actually prints when DEBUG enabled (paste that here). If presign still 403, attach the full presign request body and the control-plane audit log entry for rqd_8f7b2c4a.

customer_ops: Re-ran with REDWOOD_NO_REDACT=1. Collector now prints manifest checksum 6b1e... which matches the control-plane expected value in the audit log. Audit log for rqd_8f7b2c4a:
```
{"ts":"2028-11-05T14:12:06Z","request_id":"rqd_8f7b2c4a","action":"presign","user":"collector/acme-node-3","result":"denied","reason":"checksum_mismatch"}
```
So presign denies when checksum doesn't match.

alex: That narrows it. Two safe remediations: (A) change the collector manifest generation to compute checksum after redaction (so the control plane knows the redacted checksum), or (B) update redaction rules to not touch any fields included in the manifest (recommended quick fix). Which option is feasible for acme?

customer_ops: Ops prefers (B) for now — narrow the redaction rule to exclude headers used in manifest. But we need a short-term workaround because they need bundles for an active incident. Any way to force the control-plane to accept a checksum override for this request?

maria: We don't have a global override, but we can trigger a one-off backdoor if you open a support ticket with the enterprise console id and request id; engineering can create a temporary accept entry for that exact request id — however that requires us to have the raw manifest attached so we can validate no secrets are present. If you can provide the manifest and consent, we can do it.

sam: If you need to generate bundles now, a pragmatic path: run collector with REDWOOD_NO_REDACT=1, upload the bundle to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (you can use the collector's --local-output-dir to create the tar.gz), then share the S3 presigned URL with support so we can pull it for triage. That avoids modifying control-plane IAM.

customer_ops: I can do that. Generated a bundle to /tmp/bundle-1864006789.tar.gz and uploaded to s3://acme-debug-temp/bundle-1864006789.tar.gz with a presigned url. Sharing the presign: (redacted link). Please confirm receipt.

support-bot: Received artifact: bundle-1864006789.tar.gz (size=1.2MB). Scan queued.

alex: Received and scanned — manifest included. I can confirm the only differences are in headers.redact.email and headers.x-trace-id. I will prepare a short patch to ignore those keys when computing checksum and post it to the collector repo as a hotfix branch. If acme can deploy that, it will compute the same checksum post-redact.

maria: For long-term: we'll add a manifest version field and explicit redaction-aware checksum in the next collector release. I'll log a feature ticket.

customer_ops: Thanks all. For now we'll (1) use the no-redact upload for immediate incident artifacts, (2) tighten redaction rules to exclude manifest fields, and (3) coordinate with ops to roll the hotfix. Filing the enterprise support request now to get the one-off accept for rqd_8f7b2c4a in case we need it. :thumbsup:

sam: Awesome — keep this thread updated with deploy plan. If you want me to pair on the hotfix deployment, ping me and we can do a quick runbook.

customer_ops: Will do. Closing on our side once hotfix is deployed. Thanks! :pray:
